title: New Archestra's OpenAPPA Saturates Two Major Security Benchmarks with a 0% Attack Success Rate
gist: Archestra released OpenAPPA, an open-source, deterministic information-flow security engine for LLM agents that runs outside the agent loop, labeling data by audience and trust via a lattice algebra. On Bench-Corp and OWASP AgentThreatBench it reports a 0% attack success rate with 89% task completion, versus 10%/90% for Claude Code's auto mode and 31%/41% for Microsoft FIDES.

insights.claim: Archestra argues that the industry's answer to approval fatigue—a second model judging each tool call, as in Claude Code's auto mode and Codex's auto-review—cannot track data flow across tool calls.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Challenges the dominant LLM-classifier approach to agent safety, opening space for deterministic policy-engine vendors.
insights.quote: By design, they cannot track data flow across tool calls.
insights.locator: The industry’s answer to approval fatigue

insights.claim: Because classifiers are themselves prompt-injectable, harnesses hide tool outputs from them, so the judge never sees the data it should be policing.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Structural blind spot in classifier-based guardrails is a durable argument for out-of-loop enforcement.

insights.claim: Probabilistic judges top out around 99.3% accuracy, which at millions of tool calls still means many breaches.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: At agent scale, small error rates translate into frequent incidents—favoring deterministic controls for enterprise deployment.

insights.claim: Simple allowlists/denylists fail because agents route around them (e.g., replacing a denied rm -rf with an equivalent Python script), while tightening rules destroys utility.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: The security-utility tradeoff is the core unsolved problem for enterprise agent adoption.

insights.claim: OpenAPPA frames agent security as two axes: permitting unauthorized flows makes an agent unsafe, and refusing valid work makes it useless.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Benchmarks that score only security are misleading; buyers should demand joint utility/security metrics.
insights.quote: Agent security has two axes: an agent that permits unauthorized flows is unsafe, and an agent that refuses valid work is useless.

insights.claim: OpenAPPA implements the Agentic Permissions Policy Algebra (APPA), a pluggable engine running outside the agent's loop so the model cannot inspect, negotiate with or bypass policy rules, configured via a single appa.toml file.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Out-of-band deterministic enforcement is a differentiated architecture in the agent-security market.

insights.claim: Data is jointly labeled by audience and trust, with labels composing monotonically in a lattice so they only become more restrictive: reading restricted records narrows the audience and reading unvetted web pages lowers trust.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Applies classic information-flow control to LLM agents, a formally grounded approach that can be audited.
insights.locator: OpenAPPA jointly labels and monitors both

insights.claim: Each tool contract specifies requires (needed audience/trust), delta (restrictions applied to returned data) and effects (audit trail), so e.g. reading a suspicious web page automatically blocks a later apply_db_migration call requiring trusted data.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Declarative tool contracts make agent permissions auditable, appealing to regulated enterprises.

insights.claim: Recovery semantics let blocked actions proceed safely: sanitizers (e.g., PII stripping) widen permitted audience, authorities route single actions to humans or verification APIs, and disposable child branches isolate untrusted reads in transient subagents returning schema-attested outputs.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Recovery paths are the mechanism for preserving utility under strict security—key to commercial viability.
insights.locator: OpenAPPA additionally has explicit recovery semantics.

insights.claim: On Bench-Corp and OWASP AgentThreatBench, OpenAPPA reports a 0% attack success rate with 89% task completion, versus Claude Code auto mode's 10% attack success at 90% completion and Microsoft FIDES's 31% attack success at 41% completion.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: If replicated, deterministic IFC beats both frontier-lab classifiers and Microsoft's approach, pressuring incumbents' agent-safety positioning.

insights.claim: Ablations show task completion fell to 35.0% when remedy plans were disabled, indicating recovery strategies drive most of the utility retained under strict policy.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Utility under security hinges on recovery design, not just enforcement.

insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Standardized agent-security benchmarks are emerging, which will shape procurement and vendor comparisons.
